user.title: Choose your recipe folder
user.description: Recipe Wizard reads recipes from a folder of files on your Home Assistant machine. Tell it which folder, and it will check that it can read the recipes before saving.

data_description.recipes_dir: The folder holding your recipe files. Each recipe is one file ending in .json, and folders inside this one are searched too. If you type a name rather than a full path, it is taken as a folder next to your configuration.yaml.

reconfigure.title: Change your recipe folder
reconfigure.description: If you have moved your recipes, tell Recipe Wizard where they are now. It will check that it can read them before changing anything. Nothing is copied or moved for you, and your recipe files are not touched.

data_description.recipes_dir: The folder holding your recipe files. If you type a name rather than a full path, it is taken as a folder next to your configuration.yaml. Everything else stays as it is: your dashboard cards keep working, a cook-along in progress carries on, and your shopping list keeps its ticks.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Recipe Wizard is now reading your recipes from the new folder.

error.directory_not_found: There is no folder at {detail}. Check the spelling, or create the folder and put your recipe files in it.
error.no_recipes: No recipes were found in {detail}. Recipe Wizard looks for files ending in .json, including in folders inside this one.
error.foods_unreadable: Recipe Wizard could not read its own list of foods. That file is part of the integration rather than something you edit, so reinstalling the integration usually fixes it. The error was: {detail}
error.invalid_recipe: One of the recipe files could not be read: {detail}. Fix or move that file, then try again.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. The details are in your Home Assistant log.

foods_unreadable.message: Recipe Wizard could not read its own list of foods: {detail}

invalid_recipe.message: A recipe file could not be read: {detail}

library_not_loaded.message: Recipe Wizard has not finished reading your recipes yet. Try again in a moment.

recipe_not_found.message: No recipe matches "{recipe}". Use the recipe's name, or enough of it to tell it apart from the others.

recipe_ambiguous.message: "{recipe}" matches more than one recipe: {matches}. Say a bit more of the name.

recipe_unresolvable.message: Recipe Wizard could not work out a shopping list for {recipe}: {detail}

computed_item_read_only.message: "{item}" is worked out from your recipe, so its wording cannot be changed here. You can still tick it off, or take it off this list. To change the words, edit the recipe.

item_gone.message: "{item}" is no longer on the shopping list.

not_loaded.message: Recipe Wizard is not set up, or it cannot read your recipe folder at the moment. Check it under Settings, then Devices and services.

not_cooking.message: No cook-along is running, so there is no step to move to. Start one first.

already_finished.message: The cook-along has finished. Go back a step to read the last one again, or start another recipe.

at_the_first_step.message: You are already on the first step.

no_such_recipe.message: No recipe in your folder matches "{recipe_id}".

ambiguous_recipe.message: "{recipe_id}" matches more than one recipe: {matches}. Say which one you mean.

cook_along_failed.message: Recipe Wizard could not work out the steps for {recipe_id}: {detail}

invalid_recipe.title: Recipe Wizard cannot fully read "{name}"
invalid_recipe.description:
There are problems in the recipe file for **{name}** (`{recipe}`) that stop Recipe Wizard cooking along with it or shopping for it properly.

{findings}

Each line names the part of the recipe to fix. Recipe files are your own documents and Recipe Wizard never edits them, so open the file in a text editor, or run `python -m recipe_wizard --list --validate` to see the same list on a terminal.

This notice disappears on its own once the recipe reads cleanly — within 15 minutes of you saving it, or straight away if you reload Recipe Wizard.

set_shopping_list.name: Set shopping list
set_shopping_list.description: Chooses the recipe the shopping list is for, and how many batches of it you are making. Anything you have already ticked off is cleared, because it belonged to the previous list. Items you added yourself are kept.

recipe.name: Recipe
recipe.description: The recipe you are shopping for: its name, or enough of the name to pick out just one recipe.

batches.name: Batches
batches.description: How many batches you are making. 1 is one batch of the recipe as written; 2 doubles it, including any sub-recipes it uses.

include_optional.name: Include optional parts
include_optional.description: Turn this off to leave out the parts of the recipe marked optional, such as a sauce that goes with it. Optional ingredients inside a part you are still making are kept, because another part may need the same food.

start_cook_along.name: Start cook-along
start_cook_along.description: Starts cooking a recipe one step at a time, with every amount worked out for the batch size you are making.

recipe_id.name: Recipe
recipe_id.description: Which recipe to cook. Part of its name is enough — "brownies" — as long as it matches only one recipe. If two recipes match, you are told which.

batches.name: Batches
batches.description: How many batches to make. 1 is the recipe as written, 2 doubles it, and halves and quarters are allowed. Doubling a cake doubles its frosting too.

next_step.name: Next step
next_step.description: Moves on to the next step. After the last step the cook-along reads as finished.

previous_step.name: Previous step
previous_step.description: Goes back one step, so you can read it again.

stop_cook_along.name: Stop cook-along
stop_cook_along.description: Ends the cook-along. Nothing happens if none is running.
